posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

Two billion years ago, the world’s first nuclear reactors appeared in Oklo, Gabon. They were NOT made by humans and were self-regulating and accident-free.

In the late 9th century, Vikings have raided kingdom after kingdom and nearly conquered all of England. Wealthy monasteries and defenseless nuns were especially tempting targets and often suffered great losses. However, all of that stopped when Vikings were confronted by princess Aethelflaed, daughter of Alfred the Great.

Who was Lady of Mercia, and how did she shape the history of England by becoming Vikings' greatest nightmare? Watch our latest Nightshift video to find out! 🌚
Laughing gas can make you feel relaxed and euphoric in seconds. But it comes with serious risks as well. So, what exactly is laughing gas and why does it feel so good?

In the 17th century in Germany, one of Europe’s most terrifying witch hunts turned the town of Bamberg against itself. Tortures that occurred in the "Witch Factory" forced innocent people to name friends, neighbors and family members, creating a deadly chain reaction that eventually reached even the richest and most powerful, while those running the trials profited from the people they condemned.

How did a witch hunt grow so powerful that almost nobody was safe? And what finally brought one of
What if you could skip the boring and painful parts of life? It sounds tempting until you realize what you’d lose along the way. Time doesn’t really stop, and neither does the world.

recentPosts.caption:
A famous toilet in Thailand… for a reason you probably wouldn’t expect. 😂⁠
A bathroom surrounded by one-way glass, creating a hilarious experience for anyone inside, you can see what’s happening outside while people passing by have no idea they’re being watched.⁠
⁠
Would you actually use this bathroom? 👀⁠
🎥: @mar.nocap

China’s Ghost Festival is a traditional celebration centered around ancestors and the spirit world.⁠
⁠
Observed during the seventh month of the lunar calendar, the festival is based on the belief that spirits return to the living world during this time. ⁠
⁠
Families may prepare food, burn incense, and make paper offerings as a way to honor their ancestors and show respect to visiting spirits.⁠
⁠
The 15th day of the month, known as Zhongyuan Festival, is considered the main day of the celebration

Ever wondered what the ocean looks like from a tuna’s point of view? 🐟🌊⁠
A GoPro attached to a tuna gives us a rare glimpse beneath the surface, revealing an underwater world that’s impossible to see from above.⁠
⁠
How amazing is that?⁠
🎥: @kennyslowbird

Meet Cece, the cat who has made an ancient Egyptian temple her home.⁠
⁠
She spends her days wandering through the Temple of Dendera, appearing between the columns and courtyards while visitors explore the site.⁠
⁠
When the Egyptian heat gets too much, she usually finds a shady spot near the stone walls, where she can stay cool.⁠
⁠
Cece has become such a familiar sight that many visitors now look for her when they arrive, and she regularly ends up in their photos, too.⁠
⁠
By: @bradflowerss

One of the most iconic traditions you can witness in Athens. ⁠
At Syntagma Square, the Evzones perform the Changing of the Guard at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.⁠
⁠
Their distinctive uniforms are filled with symbolism, from the 400 pleats of the fustanella representing the centuries of Ottoman rule to the heavy pom-pom shoes known as tsarouchia.⁠
⁠
The ceremony takes place every hour, with an especially impressive full ceremony every Sunday at 11 AM.⁠
🎥: @ulkertravels

@danniculescu and @judithms take us through what might be the most scenic McDonald’s you’ll ever visit. 🍟🌴⁠
⁠
Located in Kāneʻohe on Oʻahu, this McDonald’s has a view you definitely don’t expect from a fast-food restaurant. ⁠
⁠
The Koʻolau Mountains rise right behind it, making the drive-thru look like it belongs somewhere completely different.⁠
⁠
And the Hawaii menu has a few surprises too, with regional favorites like Spam, Portuguese sausage, and rice that you won’t usually find at McDonald

Ten places where the water genuinely looks like this, and a real hotel at every one. Every property here already works with creators.

Most people assume a stay somewhere like this is years of saving away. It isn’t. Hotels have empty rooms every night and they need content constantly. They’d rather host someone who can film the place properly than let the room sit empty.

One of our members had under 500 followers in May. By August he’d landed over 10 free stays, all shot on his phone. What chan

Japan’s manhole covers are anything but ordinary.⁠
⁠
Across the country, you’ll find colorful covers with designs inspired by local culture, landmarks, flowers, animals, mascots, and even popular characters. Many designs reflect the city or region they come from, turning an everyday part of the street into something surprisingly fun to spot.⁠
⁠
Next time you’re walking around Japan, look down…you might just find one of your favorite characters under your feet.⁠
⁠
By: @kawaiilife24 @kvremkeiko

A diving experience with only one person not brave enough to take the leap! 😂🌊⁠
Friends diving into the open water while one stays safely above, cheering them on.⁠
We all have that one friend who’s ready to support the adventure… just not participate in it.⁠
⁠
Tag the friend who would be cheering your dive from up top! 👇😂⁠
🎥: @zackdell_

@geo.rock888 captured these striking photographs of people from Indonesia’s Buton Island with unusually rare eye colors.⁠
⁠
Some have vivid blue eyes, while others have two different-colored eyes. The trait has been associated with Waardenburg syndrome, a rare genetic condition that can affect pigmentation and, in some cases, hearing.⁠
⁠
Not everyone in the Buton community has the trait, making it a rare sight to witness.

A taste of old-school Macau, made the same way for generations. ⁠
This third-generation family-run restaurant has been making bamboo-pressed noodles since 1945, using a traditional technique that gives the noodles their distinctive texture.⁠
⁠
The process is especially fascinating: the dough is pressed and worked with bamboo, and the restaurant still uses a noodle press that’s nearly 60 years old. 🎋⁠
⁠
🎥: @natashaciho

A former prison in Japan now has a very different purpose.⁠
⁠
Nara Prison was built in 1908 and is one of Japan’s best-known examples of historic red-brick architecture. Today, the building has been restored and turned into a luxury hotel, while much of its original character remains.⁠
⁠⁠
By: @hoshinoya.official

Until 2025, only two adult Tyrannosaurus rex footprints had been found in the entire world—but high school teacher Kent Hups made history when he discovered the first adult T. rex trackway. Working with his close friend and National Geographic Explorer Tyler Lyson, the pair excavated a total of five footprints in North Dakota, each preserved as a 3D shape in the ancient rocks. 

Learn more about the unusual discovery at the link in bio. 

Video by Alex Wenchel

Commercial poaching killed more than 90 percent of black rhinos in Zimbabwe and across the rest of Africa, eventually leaving none in Matusadona National Park. More than 30 years after officials and conservationists worked to rescue the remaining rhinos in the Zambezi Valley, descendants of those animals have returned to the park. Photographer @marcuswestbergphotography documented their return—and quieter moments as they rested throughout the day.

Learn more about efforts to save the black rhin

Some accounts from September 11, 2001, have remained unheard for 25 years. Now, deeply personal experiences from survivors, first responders, and witnesses can be heard in 9/11: The National Geographic Video Archive. Featuring more than 100 hours of video testimony, the interactive archive can be organized by time, location, and topic for viewers to hear from those who lived through the attacks and the aftermath.

Island hopping in the Seychelles? Yes, please.

The Seychelles—an archipelago of 115 islands off the east coast of Africa—is the gift that keeps on giving for @filipe_deandrade. “Everywhere you go, every single corner you turn down, ends up being a different and more beautiful view,” he says. From swimming with sea turtles to soaking up panoramic views, each day offers up new wow-worthy moments. Spotted lanternflies first appeared in the United States in 2014 and have continued to spread in the 12 years since. The invasive species, now found across 19 states, feeds on plant sap, harms trees, and threatens the grape and wine industry as well as many other crops. While experimenting with ways to fight back against the insects, scientists have discovered a promising new weapon: milkweed.

Learn how planting milkweed could help the fight against spotted lanternflies at the link in bio.

Again and again, this young humpback whale burst from the waters off Baja California, breaching more than 50 times in roughly an hour. Captured on film by Martin Gregus Jr. @mywildlive, the calf is spending its first months in warm waters, staying close to its mother as it nurses and builds strength for the long migrations ahead.

Photos by @joelsartore | Beavers are incredible engineers. The dams they build help maintain a healthy balance within environments by controlling runoff, erosion, and floods. Because of this, their actions not only directly benefit humans but also create crucial habitats for various plant and animal species. 

Photos taken @newildliferehab, a center in Omaha, Nebraska, that saves injured and orphaned wildlife. To see more species featured in the Photo Ark, follow me @joelsartore. #PhotoArk

Before puberty, boys are more likely to have asthma, but after puberty, that pattern reverses. By adulthood, about one in 10 women in the U.S. has asthma, nearly twice the rate among men. Researchers are now getting closer to understanding that shift, including how hormones such as estrogen can influence airway inflammation and the severity of asthma symptoms.

Learn what else could be behind these differences at the link in bio.

Photograph by Rebecca Hale @beckythale

Eight years ago, photographer Pete McBride @pedromcbride almost lost his Colorado home to a wildfire. This summer, he heads back to the flames. Across the American West, an intense fire season is stretching firefighting teams thin. In Colorado, the Gold Mountain Fire has burned over 38,000 acres, while the Aspen Acres Fire has surpassed over 100,000 acres and destroyed hundreds of homes. Octopus cyanea (also known as the big blue octopus) evade predators and ambush prey by sending brain signals to pigment-filled sacks and muscle bundles, changing its skin complexion in minutes.

This is what safety in numbers looks like 🐟 🐟 🐟
 
Faced with hungry predators, thousands of fish gather into one enormous, constantly moving bait ball. The sheer numbers make it difficult for a hunter to focus on just one. Sticking together is the best defence for these fish. 
 
Revisit 25 years of extraordinary ocean stories from Blue Planet with us. Find out where to watch the full series via the link in our bio 🔗
 
#BluePlanet #25Anniversary #MarineAnimals #Underwater

The ocean floor is full of surprises 👀
 
Hidden in plain sight on the seafloor, angel sharks are built for ambush. They can stay buried in the sand for days before lunging at passing prey, but even perfect camouflage doesn’t guarantee a successful strike. 
 
Celebrate 20 years of Planet Earth with us. Find out where to watch the full episode via our link in bio 💚

#PlanetEarth #DavidAttenborough #PE20 #PEIII

The solar system isn’t for the faint-hearted 🌌 🪐

From the scorching surface of Venus to the volcanic chaos of Io, our solar system is home to some truly hostile worlds. 

Discover which could be the scariest place of all via the link in bio.

#SolarSystem #Planets #Venus #Jupiter

Bet you didn’t see that coming 👀
 
Buried beneath the sand, angel sharks can lie perfectly camouflaged and wait for days for prey to swim by. Once a fish gets close enough, they burst from the seabed to strike. But does this technique always work?
 
Celebrate 20 years of Planet Earth with us. Find out where to watch the full episode via our link in bio 💚

Inspired by the extraordinary stories and iconic animals featured in Evolution, explore the collection and shop with Teemill via the link in our bio.
 
#Evolution #Merch #Design #Tshirt

Finding your feet 👣

Over 500 million years ago, flecks of food drifting on ocean currents were eaten by small animals on the seabed, but the flow would often change. To reach them, some tried a pioneering action: they would move. These are thought to be some of the first animal tracks on Earth.

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

Who knew the ocean has a public transport system 🦀
 
Columbus crabs aren’t built for long-distance swimming, so this little crab takes a shortcut through the open ocean. By hitchhiking a ride on a turtle, he find transport, a new home and some unexpected company.
 
Celebrate 20 years of Planet Earth with us. Find out where to watch the full episode via our link in bio 💚

More than meets the eye 👀

Ancient ancestors of the dolphin hid from the sun’s UV rays using two light-detecting spots. Fascinatingly, some inherited mutations that allowed them to perceive light and shade together, so they could visualise their environment - essentially becoming the first proper eyes.

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

Evolution presenter @chrisgpackham2 reveals how coming face-to-face with some extraordinary bats fulfilled a childhood dream.

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

Turns out the forest has a group chat 📞
 
Treehoppers might be tiny, but they’ve got plenty to say! They communicate through vibrations sent along the plants they live on, most of which are too quiet for us to hear. But when danger appears, sending the right signal can make all the difference.
